problems: The new lookups refine binding predictions but do not establish TF occupancy at the variant: E25 is a strong ETS2 own-model prediction, while E26 is a TFAP2E own-model prediction favoring G with only a small change in site-strength percentiles. Both remain in-vitro predictions.
E27 is explicitly not tested: TFAP2E was not assayed in the searched ENCODE biosamples, and absence of a ReMap peak is not evidence against binding.
The element-to-IRF6 link remains indirect. The cited IRF6 eQTL is in cerebellum, the cleft L2G support is modest, and the element links do not demonstrate causal IRF6 regulation.

The cleft risk allele is A, whereas H1, H2, and H5 predict greater TF binding to G. This is not a demonstrated contradiction because no effect of binding on IRF6 expression or disease risk is established; for H3 and H4, greater binding to A likewise does not establish the downstream direction.
The element is inactive in the inferred tibial-nerve context, and no cleft-relevant active cell type is established. The aggregate cCRE activity maxima do not identify a relevant biosample.

games.reason: Both chains lack TF ChIP-seq evidence at the variant, so neither has direct occupancy support (E13, E14). B is better supported by the TF-specific evidence shown: ZNF76 has higher expression in the stated context (32.4 TPM versus TFAP2E at 7.1 TPM), and its model predicts a clearer ref-over-alt binding difference (99.4th versus 85.9th percentile). TFAP2E’s own model predicts only a very small site-strength difference (89.1st versus 89.6th percentile); the stronger AP-2 family predictions are not TFAP2E-specific (E13, E14, E26). This is a relative preference, not direct evidence for either mechanism.

The shared element, target-gene, cell-type, and phenotype evidence does not distinguish the chains. The binding evidence favors A: the ZNF76 model predicts appreciably stronger binding to A than G (ref 99.4th vs alt 85.9th percentile), whereas TFAP2E’s own model predicts only a negligible percentile difference (ref 89.1st vs alt 89.6th). A’s stronger-binding allele also matches the reported cleft association effect allele A; B predicts stronger binding to G. Neither chain has variant-site ChIP-seq evidence, and the not-tested TFAP2E result is not evidence against B.
